subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmeai.com>, Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@acmeai.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Hi Samir / Taylor,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the context on Acme AI's multi-tenant scaling pain. Quick recap from our side to make sure we're aligned and call out next steps.

Key pain points you shared:
- No tenant-level rate limiting today; a small number of high-volume customers are causing noisy-neighbor behavior that spikes tail latency for everyone.
- Need per-customer quotas and tiering (free / standard / premium) to enforce billing and protect SLOs.
- Desire to route premium customers to dedicated capacity or higher-priority pools during peak windows.
- Need visibility (per-tenant latency/cost breakdown) and a simple billing export for your finance stack.

Current stack notes you gave:
- Backend: AWS EKS + Kong API gateway in front
- Currently using OpenAI for generation, ~50M tokens/month total, top 5 customers account for ~40% of traffic
- Token accounting and billing currently done in-house via batch jobs

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Reduce noisy-neighbor incidents / tail-latency regressions by ~90% for standard customers
- Ability to set per-tenant monthly and burst quotas and enforce them automatically
- Route top-tier customers to dedicated/different model pools with measurable latency improvements
- Exportable usage CSV for billing integration

Proposed next steps:
1) Sharing a short technical spec that outlines how Redwood enforces per-tenant rate limiting, quotas, and routing (attached).
2) Schedule a 60-minute SE deep-dive next week to map a POC (I proposed times below). Marcus (our SE) will join to discuss implementation patterns.
3) Exchange sample telemetry (anonymized request/tenant IDs & traffic profile) so we can give an initial config recommendation and estimate savings.

Attachments: redwood-multi-tenant-controls-spec.pdf (high-level controls + config examples), mutual-action-plan-acme.xlsx (proposed timeline).

Proposed SE deep-dive slots:
- Wed 2026-06-17 10:00–11:00 PT
- Thu 2026-06-18 08:00–09:00 PT

If the above looks right, I’ll loop Marcus in and lock a slot.
\Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmeai.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Thanks Lauren — this is a great summary and matches what we discussed. A couple clarifications / additions from our side:

- Routing: we currently do lightweight routing at Kong (header-based) but we don’t have per-tenant model pool assignment. We’d like the option to route only the top 10 customers to dedicated pools.
- Quotas: monthly token quotas + short burst allowances are critical; we also want admin overrides per-account.
- Billing integration: we use Stripe and would prefer a near-real-time usage export (daily).
- Security: we’ll need to see a brief on how keys are handled and whether telemetry can be scrubbed.
- Timeline: procurement/end-to-end POC target is end of Q3 (Sept). We’re aiming to have a pilot with 2 customers by mid-August.

We can do the Wed 6/17 10am PT slot. I’ll invite our product lead Taylor if that’s OK.

Samir

Head of Platform, Acme AI
samir.patel@acmeai.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls (rate limits, quotas, per-customer routing)

Hi Samir / Lauren — Marcus from Redwood SE team here, thanks for the intro. A few technical thoughts to prepare for the SE deep-dive and to make the POC smooth:

1) Enforcement model:
- Edge enforcement: configure per-tenant rate limits at Kong (or the API edge) for immediate protection; this is low-friction but limited visibility.
- Server-side enforcement: Redwood enforces per-tenant token quotas and burst logic within the runtime with consistent accounting; we expose per-tenant metrics for latency/cost.

2) Routing / tiering:
- We can map tenant metadata to routing policies: route premium tenants to a dedicated pool (pinned GPU nodes) or to a higher-priority queue in shared pools.
- Recommend a hybrid approach: small number of pinned pools for top customers + model-variant fallbacks for cost control.

3) Token accounting and billing:
- Redwood supports daily usage exports (CSV/JSON) with tenant IDs and token counts suitable for Stripe ingestion.

4) Data & SEC compliance:
- We support key management integrations (KMS) and have options to redact PII from telemetry. For your security team, we can provide a short appendix on key handling (will attach).

Next steps for the call: please share an anonymized sample of tenant traffic (headers, request rates, distribution) and any current Kong policies. I’ll prepare a config example and a POC plan to present.

Looking forward — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
